title: Career summary: first drums to Celestin's band
summary: Barbarin sums up how he got Paul's drums, sat in with Sam Morgan and Kid Rena, joined the Imperial Serenaders, the Steamer Capitol, Celestin, Desvigne and the 1947 USO tour.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I learned drums by playing on my mother's chairs, the two forks. That was in the year of 1916. My father bought my brother, Paul, a set of drums. And Paul was playing around here with different bands. And he was called to Chicago to play with Manuel Ferrer's band at the Royal Garden in Chicago. My first set of drums was the one Paul was working with in Chicago. And he sent them to me because he bought some new ones. Well, I was on the way to start playing the first job. I played a house party, just a piano and drums. The musicians around here heard how well I was playing and hired me to play with them. They were not organized. And I would go to different dances. And Sam Morgan's band and Kid René's band were playing. And they would let me sit in and play with them. I became known. The name bands would start hiring me. Sam Morgan, Kid René, Jack Carey, Kid Punch, AJ Piron's band. I played at Tom Anderson's Night Spot in 1923 on Rampart Street near Canal in the Red Light District. The years of 1923, an organized band named Imperial Serenaders gave me my break. I played with them around here a while. And they'd taken a job at the Victory Inn, a night spot on the Jefferson Highway. Albert Snider, the trumpet man who was in charge of the band, had a day job. And he said he would not quit to play at night. So at that time, Sidney Desvane had came in from St. Louis off the Steamer Capital. And he'd taken a job playing trumpet in the band. And the band's name was changed to Sudden Syncopator. We played on the Steamer Capital and the Island Queen of Cincinnati. Red Island and Pop Foster was with the band at that time. I started playing with Poppa Celestine's band in 1937. And in the 40s, I started with Sidney Desvane's band again. In 1947, I went to New York with Danny Barker, speculating on his job. And I got the USO group. Was going to Japan. So I made the trip. Played Manila Okinawa in Japan. June 1948. I was back in the States. Started back with Sidney's band until 1950. Then I joined Poppa Celestine's band. We were playing at the Paddock Lounge. And I quit because I did not think much of the job. So I went to work at the Elmer Rock with Joy Lewis' group. And I played with them six months. The job closed. And I went to a famous dole. And played there about three months. And the contract ended. I went back with Celestine's group. And here I am.
